title: Assert digit interpolation in he.todaysLearning(5) test — it only checks isNotEmpty while the EN counterpart checks contains('3')
why: The EN test explicitly verifies the {count} placeholder is substituted into the rendered string; the HE test for the identical method only checks isNotEmpty. If a translator or a bad ARB edit drops the {count} placeholder from lib/l10n/app_he.arb's todaysLearning message (leaving a static 'לימוד היום' with no digit), the HE test still passes while the equivalent EN regression would fail. In a bilingual app where Hebrew is the RTL-primary locale, the weaker locale currently gets the weaker regression check.
recommendation: Change line 81 to `expect(he.todaysLearning(5), contains('5'))` to match the rigor of the EN test at line 49.
acceptance_criteria: he.todaysLearning(5) test asserts contains('5') (or an equivalent digit-presence check), not just isNotEmpty
Test fails if lib/l10n/app_he.arb's todaysLearning message loses its {count} placeholder on regeneration
